cases.purpose: Real enemy-environment damage carrying sourceID -1 normalizes to a null source with the NO_ACTOR_SENTINEL reason, and no ActorRef -1 is ever minted. The four events also share one timestamp, so the count check doubles as proof that equal timestamps are not collapsed.

rationale.text: The -1 sentinel contract is owned by the normalization layer and is evidence-backed: the mid-fight window capture carries 92 events with sourceID -1 and 117 with targetID -1, including environment damage with no stated source. Reading -1 as an actor id would mint a well-formed actor that exists nowhere in master data.

limitations: Says nothing about negative values other than -1; that is the derived case's job.

cases.purpose: A sanitized slice whose SUBSET_SELECTION retained no coverage cannot prove that an actor never cast anything. Asked for actor 14's last completed cast over the whole window, the state layer must answer UNKNOWN for INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE — never EXACT null, which would be a proven absence manufactured from trimming.

rationale.text: Absence claims are gated on COMPLETE coverage of the interval (state-result.ts). The harness grants coverage only from the artifact's retainedCoverage, which is empty because the transformation record says so. CLAUDE.md: partial event retrieval does NOT mean the player performed no events during the missing interval.

limitations: Pins the reason INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE, which presumes the CASTS category is OBSERVABLE from captures. If the harness ever stopped granting capability to captures the reason would move to CAPABILITY_UNVERIFIED, and this case should fail so the change is reviewed.

cases.purpose: A negative source id that is not the verified sentinel is recorded as UNUSABLE_VALUE — neither an actor nor a 'no actor' statement — while the untouched sentinel events in the same payload keep their NO_ACTOR_SENTINEL meaning. Proves the rule discriminates rather than treating all negatives alike.

rationale.text: No evidence supports generalising -1's meaning. The normalization layer therefore records an unobserved negative as something it cannot interpret, and refuses to build an actor from it. The artifact is DERIVED: the -5 is constructed, and the case claims only how the layer treats it, not that it occurs.

limitations: The mutated event was never observed; this is a rule-of-the-layer claim, not a capture claim.

cases.purpose: The resource snapshot attached to a costed COMPLETE cast is tagged PRE_COST with amount, max and cost preserved verbatim; an uncosted cast on the same actor stays EVENT_ASSOCIATED with a null cost. The finisher's 7/7 costing 7 is the cap-bounded falsifier of the post-cost reading.

rationale.text: amount == max while cost > 0 is decided from one event with no arithmetic: a post-cost reading would require holding max + cost, above the cap. The wider investigation behind the fixture found 126 cap-bounded falsifiers and zero counterexamples across 423 costed entries in two reports. The timing tag itself is owned by the resource layer and decided once from the normalized model.

limitations: Establishes PRE_COST for costed COMPLETE casts only. resourcechange stays EVENT_ASSOCIATED because its evidence rests on same-timestamp adjacency.
Does not make the post-cost amount knowable.

cases.purpose: An event whose type string no evidence-backed contract recognises is preserved as an UNSUPPORTED_TYPE event and counted under its verbatim type string. It is not dropped, and it is not coerced into a known family.

rationale.text: Only evidence-backed types are contracted (supported-families.ts). Anything else must fail closed as explicitly unsupported rather than disappear, because a dropped event would read downstream as an event that never happened.

limitations: Synthetic input. Proves the path, not any real Warcraft Logs type.

cases.purpose: A ReportEventPaginator whose data is null decodes to MALFORMED_PAGINATOR. 'We could not read your events' must never become 'you produced no events'.

rationale.text: The decoder owns the classification and documents it in place: data: JSON is nullable upstream, and a null or non-array payload is a malformed page, never an empty one. The paginator then records the stream PARTIAL with MALFORMED_PAGE rather than an empty period.

limitations: Exercises the decoder over a decoded data object, not a raw HTTP body; transport-level parsing failures are a separate boundary.
